title: every-component-declares-its-public-interface
intention: Every component declares its public interface in its charter, and one sieve in build_inspector reds any import from one component into another that does not land in the target's declared interface — a device's interface being the bus plus any client tool it publishes.
why: RULE 1 (Akien, 2026-10-01; agreed text on CairnCommons/tickets/8e3474a6ae43-rule-1-encapsulation.json): every component talks to every other only through its public interface — so a change stays inside the component that made it.
traces_to: RULE 1 (ticket 8e3474a6ae43, Akien's agreed text: 'Physics: one check over every component reds any reach past a public interface, the moment it is written' and agreed detail 1: 'Public interfaces are DECLARED EXPLICITLY. A component lists its public surface, and anything not listed is internal.'); Law 4 (a rule that matters is physics); supersedes ticket 7b5c539cb58c (the tool/skill face) whose WRONG INTENT branch Akien's answer closed.
how: Charter field `public_interface`: a list of dotted module names other components may import. Rule, one predicate: a site in component S landing on module M in component T (S != T) holds iff M is in T's public_interface AND, when T is a device or inside device D while S is outside D, T is a tool nested in D whose charter says `published_by_device: true`. Component = innermost directory holding intention+why.json, across cairn/, skills/, bin/, launchers/ and the rest of the repo; proofs and probes are inside their component and are NOT skipped. A missing public_interface field is itself a finding. Built as `encapsulation_holds` in cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py over import_sieve.import_sites (child 1a), attributed to the reaching component's census row, with breaches whose reacher sits outside the census (skills/, bin/, launchers/) attributed to the target's row and the rest reported beside unbuilt_intentions. It supersedes device_isolation_holds and machine_imports_no_device (both removed in the same act, their rule now a strict subset). First declarations: each component's interface is the set of its modules other components import today across a boundary RULE 1 allows (shared tool/machine/skill, or inside one device); every into-device reach is NOT declared — it stays red until its child ticket clears it.
falsifier: RED if: (1) a fixture tool importing a device's internal module is not red; (2) a fixture skill importing a top-level tool module NOT in that tool's public_interface is not red, and the same import is red once declared; (3) a fixture proof importing another device is not red (the instrument skip is gone); (4) a fixture importing a device-nested tool marked published_by_device, through a declared module, is red; (5) a component with no public_interface field is not red; (6) device_isolation_holds or machine_imports_no_device still stand in SIEVES; (7) the first live run's into-device findings differ from the census by more than the lines moved since 2026-10-01 (51 code + 252 instrument into-device sites measured). WRONG INTENT if a declared interface has to list a module whose only importers reach it from outside its device. Horizon: the first live inspector run after the build commit.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [FIXME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> PROVED
watchme: none, because the sieve is itself the standing measurement — it runs in every pass of cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py and reds a new reach the moment the next pass reads it, so a watch would learn nothing the pass does not already say
children: none, because the sieve, its declaration field and the supersession are one predicate at one address (cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py); the resolution primitive it reads is the sibling ticket import-sieve-resolves-where-an-import-lands under parent 8e3474a6ae43, a dependency not a child
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Where? cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py: new `encapsulation_holds(row, comp_dir)` beside the two sieves it replaces; sieves/encapsulation_holds.json (band 1, record); delete sieves/device_isolation_holds.json and both functions and their SIEVES entries. (2) The scan? `_encapsulation_breaches(repo_root)` computed ONCE per inspect() (module-level cache keyed by repo_root, reset at the top of inspect()): components = dirs with intention+why.json under repo_root (SKIP_DIRS); comp_of(file) = innermost; for each import_sieve.import_sites site with target, S=comp_of(file), T=comp_of(target), skip if None or S==T; device_of(c) = first two parts after cairn/devices/ i.e. 'cairn/devices/<d>'; module M = site['module'] resolved form = import_sieve.module_name(target). Breach if M not in T's public_interface, or if device_of(T) and device_of(T)!=device_of(S) and not (T!=device_of(T) and charter(T).published_by_device is True). (3) Attribution? row dir is relative to cairn/; a breach is returned by the row whose 'cairn/'+row['dir'] == S, else (S not a census row) by the row == T; breaches where neither is a row go into a new inspect() key `encapsulation_outside_census` and make `clean` false. (4) Missing field? a census row whose charter lacks public_interface (not a list of str) yields one finding; non-census components with a missing field go to encapsulation_outside_census. (5) First declarations? a one-shot script in the scratchpad computes, per component, sorted modules reached by breaches that are NOT device-boundary breaches, and writes each charter's public_interface through `cairn artifact write <charter> --verb charter --why '<ticket id>: first public_interface declaration, measured' --from <tmp>` — read each charter first and refuse to overwrite an existing public_interface field. Devices get [] plus what their own nested components import from them. (6) Proof? cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_encapsulation_holds.py with scratch repos (tempfile, prefix encapsulation_fixture_) — one tooth per falsifier clause 1-6, plus 'old sieves' fixtures stay red. (7) Done? sealed green, and the first live run's counts recorded on the ticket as measured_at_build.

decisions.text: STEP 1 — the proof, first, run red. File cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_encapsulation_holds.py, shaped like its sibling test_machine_imports_no_device.py: sys.path gets parents[4]; the subject is resolved LATE through that file's _Late class pattern (copy the 10-line class) so a hollow revert prints red teeth instead of dying at import; named teeth def test_*(), _main() prints '  PASS  <name>' per tooth and 'green — ...', exit 0, and a failing tooth prints '  FAIL  <name>: <why>' and exit 1. Fixture: _repo(files: dict[str,str]) writes a scratch repo under tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='encapsulation_fixture_holds_') whose files live under cairn/ (charters are intention+why.json JSON text; every fixture charter carries public_interface unless the tooth is about its absence). The subject call is inspector.encapsulation_breaches(repo_root: str) -> list[dict], each {file,line,module,source,target,reason} with source/target the repo-relative component dirs and reason one of 'undeclared'|'into_device'|'missing_field'. Teeth = the intent's RED clauses: (1) cairn/tools/t imports cairn.devices.d.internal (d declares public_interface []) -> one breach reason into_device; (2) skills/s imports cairn.tools.t.priv with t declaring ['cairn.tools.t.pub'] -> breach undeclared; rewrite t's charter to declare priv -> no breach; (3) cairn/tools/t/proofs/test_x.py imports cairn.devices.d.internal -> breach (proofs are not skipped); (4) cairn/devices/d/tools/client declares published_by_device true and public_interface ['cairn.devices.d.tools.client.client'], cairn/tools/t imports that module -> no breach, and importing cairn.devices.d.tools.client.other -> breach undeclared; (5) a charter with no public_interface -> breach missing_field for that component; (6) 'device_isolation_holds' and 'machine_imports_no_device' are not keys of inspector.SIEVES and 'encapsulation_holds' is; plus (7) old-sieve fixtures stay red: cairn/devices/a importing cairn.devices.b.x, and cairn/machines/m importing cairn.devices.db_domain.store, both breach into_device (the db_domain exemption is gone). Run at the pre-build commit: every tooth FAILs on the missing name.
decisions.step: unlisted: write cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_encapsulation_holds.py first and run it red

decisions.text: STEP 2 — the sieve. In cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py, replacing _DEVICE_ISOLATION, device_isolation_holds, _MACHINE_ISOLATION and machine_imports_no_device in place: (a) encapsulation_breaches(repo_root: str) -> list[dict]: components = sorted dirs (repo-relative) holding intention+why.json found by os.walk with import_sieve.SKIP_DIRS pruned; comp_of(path) = the longest component dir that is a parent of path (None if none); charter(c) = json of c/intention+why.json ({} if unreadable); device_of(c) = 'cairn/devices/<d>' when c starts with 'cairn/devices/<d>' else None. For every component whose charter lacks public_interface as a list of str: one breach {source:c, target:c, reason:'missing_field', file:c+'/intention+why.json', line:0, module:None}. For each site in import_sieve.import_sites(repo_root) with a target: S=comp_of(site file), T=comp_of(target); skip if S is None or T is None or S==T; M=import_sieve.module_name(target); if device_of(T) and device_of(T)!=device_of(S) and not (T!=device_of(T) and charter(T).get('published_by_device') is True): reason 'into_device'; elif M not in (charter(T).get('public_interface') or []): reason 'undeclared'; else no breach. Sites of kind 'opaque' are counted in the return's sibling, never breached. (b) a module-level _BREACH_CACHE dict keyed by repo_root, cleared at the top of inspect(); _breaches(root) fills it once per pass. (c) encapsulation_holds(row, comp_dir): repo_root = the parent of the census root (the dir that holds the 'cairn' package); here = 'cairn/'+row['dir']; returns one _finding('encapsulation_holds', row['component'], '<file>:<line> imports <module> — <reason>: <target>', expected=True, actual=False, file=..., source=..., target=..., reason=...) per breach whose source == here, plus per breach whose source is not a census row ('cairn/'+r['dir'] over device_census rows, computed once) and whose target == here. (d) inspect() gains key 'encapsulation_outside_census' on the whole-repo sweep: breaches where neither source nor target is a census row; 'clean' also requires it empty. (e) SIEVES: drop the two old names, add 'encapsulation_holds'. New declaration sieves/encapsulation_holds.json = {"name":"encapsulation_holds","band":1,"band_name":"record","dials":{}}. The old sieve's declaration json, its proof test_machine_imports_no_device.py and its seal go to bin/cmd/trash (never rm). Corrected count: 83 charters repo-wide (63 under cairn/: the 62 census rows plus devices/codemother/0/tools/charter), not 97.
decisions.step: unlisted: write encapsulation_holds and its cached scan into inspector.py; retire the two isolation sieves

decisions.text: STEP 3 — the baseline. finding_baseline.json: drop the one 'known' entry (method machine_imports_no_device at machines/build_inspector, ticket 135a905eac3c) leaving "known": [] and "updated": the build date. In proofs/test_finding_baseline_reconcile.py change _COVERED's method to "encapsulation_holds" (the reconcile proof only needs a method name that exists in SIEVES); run it green.

decisions.text: STEP 5 — the live horizon. Commit, then run PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m cairn.machines.build_inspector.inspector and, independently, re-run the census script (scratchpad census.py, its from-import double count fixed by reading import_sites) over the same commit. The set of (file, line, target component) of encapsulation_holds findings with reason into_device must equal the census's into-device edge set exactly; record both counts and the equality on the ticket as measured_at_build. A difference is a red, investigated, never explained.

decisions.text: D1 addendum: the _Late class is verbatim at cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_machine_imports_no_device.py lines 22-35 (an __init__ storing the dotted module name, a __getattr__ that importlib.import_module()s it and getattr()s the name), bound as _inspector = _Late("cairn.machines.build_inspector.inspector"); copy it and the _tooth(name, fn) runner from test_finding_baseline_reconcile.py (prints '  green <name>' or '  RED   <name>: <exc>'). The retired proof carries PROVES = {"76639374d9f9": {"a": "a_machine_importing_a_device_reds_by_file_and_module"}} for PROVED ticket 76639374d9f9 (openai_wire); the new proof carries that same PROVES key and names its old-sieve tooth (7b, cairn/machines/m importing a device) exactly a_machine_importing_a_device_reds_by_file_and_module, so the coverage the PROVED ticket leans on moves with the rule rather than vanishing; the new proof's own clauses go under PROVES["56d1aff4455e"] keyed "1".."6" to the tooth names.

D2 addendum: the census rows come from 'from cairn.tools.orient.orient import device_census' (already imported by inspector.py; device_census(root=root)["measured"]["components"]). repo_root is the repository checkout directory (the parent of the 'cairn' package dir; inspect()'s root is <repo_root>/cairn). Retired files are removed with git rm (the cairn repo is git; bin/cmd/trash is only for ~/.cairn). encapsulation_breaches returns only the breach list; opaque sites are not returned by it at all — a second function encapsulation_opaque(repo_root) -> list[dict] returns the import_sites records of kind 'opaque' whose file sits in a component, and inspect() reports its length as 'encapsulation_opaque_sites' (a count, never a red) on the whole-repo sweep.

D3 addendum: _COVERED is a module-level dict at cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_finding_baseline_reconcile.py line 36: _COVERED = {"method": "machine_imports_no_device", "at": "machines/build_inspector"}; the edit replaces the method string only, giving {"method": "encapsulation_holds", "at": "machines/build_inspector"}.

D5 addendum: the independent census is the scratch script census_check.py (scratchpad, never committed): for each import_sieve.import_sites(repo_root) site with a target, S/T = innermost dir holding intention+why.json for file/target, keep when S != T and T starts with 'cairn/devices/<d>' and S does not start with that same 'cairn/devices/<d>'; collect the set of (file, line, T). The inspector side is the same triple from each encapsulation_holds finding with reason 'into_device' plus encapsulation_outside_census entries of that reason. The ticket gains, through cairn artifact write --verb cast, measured_at_build = {"commit": <sha>, "inspector_into_device": N, "census_into_device": N, "equal": true|false, "at": <ISO time>}; false is a red.

D4 addendum, the script spelled out: charters = sorted(p for p in Path(repo_root).rglob('intention+why.json') if not any(part in SKIP_DIRS for part in p.parts)) using import_sieve.sieve.SKIP_DIRS (the same pruning encapsulation_breaches walks); component(p) = p.parent relative to repo_root as posix. legal = defaultdict(set); for b in encapsulation_breaches(repo_root): if b['reason'] == 'undeclared': legal[b['target_component']].add(b['module']). For each charter path: text = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'); if '"public_interface"' in text: print('kept', path, json.loads(text)['public_interface']); continue; decl = sorted(legal.get(component(path), set())); assert text.rstrip().endswith('}'); body = text.rstrip()[:-1].rstrip(); new = body + ',
  "public_interface": ' + json.dumps(decl) + '
}
'; json.loads(new) must parse (else stop loud, write nothing); artifact.write(str(path), new, verb='charter', why='56d1aff4455e: first public_interface declaration, measured (RULE 1)'). Print one line per charter: path, len(decl). The script is census-free: the count of charters written plus kept must equal len(charters).

D5 consolidated: the independent census script for step 5 is census_check.py, DEFINED IN decision n=9 (the D5 addendum) — read D5 and n=9 together as one step: n=9 gives the script's selection rule and the measured_at_build record shape; D5 gives when it runs (after the step-4 commit, over that same commit) and that the equality is the horizon. Nothing else defines census_check.py; the older census.py named in D5's text is superseded by census_check.py.

D4 addendum correction: the breach record's keys are those D2 defines — source, target, reason, file, line, module — so the script reads legal[b['target']].add(b['module']); there is no 'target_component' key. component(path) returns the same repo-relative posix form D2's components use, so the dictionary lookup lines up.
